chase1.motion: One continuous shot at bumper height, chasing the red sedan down the wet cobbles. [0-5s] The sedan accelerates hard, its rear squatting on its springs, tyres smoking and skittering over the tram rail, while sparks keep raining from the same spot on the girder overhead. [5-8s] The camera swerves right at speed; the riveted pillar rushes up and passes inches from the lens, its black iron filling the frame.
chase1.ends_on: Full-frame black iron from the pillar passing the lens, cut inside the black.
chase1.why: Timed beats give the car's weight time to read before a physical object, already in the frame, closes the shot.

chase2.motion: Locked off on the rooftop beside the water tank, no camera movement for six seconds. Far below, the yellow roadster slides sideways across the junction, tail swinging out and dust trailing, straightens with a lurch, and runs left. The black sedan brakes and turns after it, the green tram rolls steadily on, and pedestrians hurry clear. Steam drifts; the city lights hold steady. In the last two seconds, the camera whips left and down past the tank's iron leg, smearing to blur at the peak. One continuous shot.
chase2.ends_on: Peak leftward motion blur past the tank's leg, travelling the same way as the roadster, ready to cut into a shot moving in that direction.
chase2.why: A still, distant camera keeps the cars small and credibly heavy, so the single whip at the end hits harder.

chase3.motion: Camera tracks alongside at the same speed, one continuous shot. The teal sedan fishtails on the ice, its heavy back end stepping out and catching, its crates shifting against the windows as spray blasts from the rear wheels. It pulls ahead, sliding out of frame left. The police motorcycle and sidecar skid outward, directly toward the camera, until the rider's headlamp swings into the lens and blooms to white. His hands stay on the bars.
chase3.ends_on: The motorcycle's headlamp flaring the whole frame white, cut on the flare into the next shot's brightest light.
chase3.why: The handover from sedan to motorcycle gives the side-on tracking shot a reason to end in the headlamp, so the flare is a motivated exit.

chase4.motion: The camera stays fixed to the car's interior, moving only as the cabin jolts. The car bounces over cobbles; the man grips the seat back and is thrown sideways, and the oranges drop, bounce on the velvet and roll along the seat under gravity. Through the oval window, the motorcycle closes in as market stalls fall behind. Then the car swings hard under a stone railway arch: darkness sweeps through the cabin, and black stone slides across the oval window until it fills it. One continuous shot, with the rider's hands on the handlebars.
chase4.ends_on: Cabin and oval window both gone to black under the arch, cut on that black.
chase4.why: Tying the camera to the car lets every jolt and rolling orange prove the speed and weight, with no need to show the tyres.

pov1.motion: One continuous first-person shot from the driver's eyes, fast, no cuts. [0-3s] The heavy open car charges down the cobbles, the bonnet shaking; barrels bounce towards us off the truck ahead and burst on the stones, sparks kicking up. [3-6s] Both gloved hands haul the wheel left, the whole car leaning and lurching on its springs as the biggest barrel slides past the right side of the windscreen. [6-8s] The swerve carries us at the left-hand green iron girder, which rushes up and passes right against the lens, filling the frame with black. Signs stay unreadable.
pov1.ends_on: The green girder crosses the lens and the frame is fully black; cut inside that dark.
pov1.why: A swerve around the barrel is the one action, and it physically causes the girder wipe, so the transition is earned by the driving.

pov2.motion: The camera stays perfectly still at the driver's eye for six seconds, looking out of the side window of the idling car, which trembles slightly with the engine. Behind the policeman the theatre crowd mills and laughs, and the marquee bulbs chase. He stands in profile, mouth closed on his cigarette, smoke drifting. The red glow on his cheek turns green. The glove on the door tightens. Then, in the last two seconds, the camera whips hard to the right past his profile and across the dark window pillar, smearing everything into streaks of light. Nobody speaks. Lettering stays unreadable. A single unbroken shot.
pov2.ends_on: The whip pan to the right at peak blur, streaks of light crossing the dark pillar; cut at the peak.
pov2.why: Six seconds of held nerve make the sudden whip feel like the driver's eyes snapping away, giving a fast film one tense breath.

pov3.motion: The car is already in the air, having left the raised bridge deck, and for a moment it hangs weightless above the green river, the wind flicking the driver's cuffs. The engine's weight then wins: the long cream bonnet tips slowly downward, the horizon and skyline climb out of the top of the frame, and the far tilted deck of the drawbridge swells towards us. The gloved hands stay locked on the wheel. Far below, the barge keeps moving and the water stays calm. The dark planks fill the whole view. On impact the car slams down and the view jolts once, hard. Filmed as one shot.
pov3.ends_on: Dark deck fills the frame and the car slams onto it with one hard jolt; cut on the impact, matching a jolt at the start of the next shot.
pov3.why: Told as gravity acting on a heavy car, so the fall has weight and the camera move comes from the nose dropping rather than from a floating camera.

pov4.motion: Looking backward over the rear seat of the fleeing open car, the camera bouncing with the cobbles, the alley shrinks away behind us. The driver in the tweed cap keeps glaring back, her glove clamped on the leather. The black car behind accelerates through the spilled lemons, scattering them, its nose dipping and rising on its suspension, the torn shirt flapping on its radiator. The woman in the apron shakes her fists. Laundry swings in our wake. The big crimson sheet overhead sags, then drops, slowly at first, and spreads over the lens until red cloth covers everything. Single shot, faces stay the same, no words appear.
pov4.ends_on: The crimson sheet covers the lens completely, a full frame of red cloth with light through the weave; cut there onto a red shape or light.
pov4.why: Every moving layer is pushed back by the car's speed, so the frame reads as a real chase and the falling sheet arrives as the last thing it knocks loose.

The driver stamps the throttle: the tail squats, the rear tyres bite and throw dirt, and the car pulls away out of frame right, pursued by the yellow truck. The camera, too slow, is left behind in the plume as the dust wall rolls left to right across the lens until the whole frame is pale dust. Engine noise only.
rods1.ends_on: Full-frame pale dust with no car or horizon visible, ready to cut to the next shot's camera clearing steam, smoke or fog.
rods1.why: The car's own acceleration makes the dust wall arrive, so the white-out has a physical cause and shows the weight of the car squatting.

rods2.why: Holding still for six seconds lets the tiny distant cars read as real speed and scale, so the sudden whip hits harder when it comes.

rods3.motion: The camera is bolted to the back of a car ahead, so the black bumper bar stays fixed in the foreground and everything shudders with the cobbles. The green roadster chases hard down the wet tram tracks, closing the gap the whole time. Its nose pitches over each bump, the scraping chassis throws sparks from the rail, and the driver hauls on the wheel. The right headlamp keeps growing until its white glare blooms over the lens and fills the frame. The left lamp stays dead. Shop signs stay soft and unreadable. Continuous shot, no cuts.
rods3.ends_on: The live headlamp's round white flare filling the frame, ready to match into a bright round lamp in the next shot.
rods3.why: A rigid bumper mount makes the shake do the speed and turns the closing gap into the single action, so the flare is simply the car getting too close.

rods4.motion: Camera low and still at water level in the concrete channel. The turquoise roadster charges straight at us through the shallow water, heavy, its tyres ploughing up sheets of spray that fall back with real weight, and sunset reflections break apart in its wake. The yellow car stays up on the sloped wall behind it, tilted, and the men in hats stay on the ledge. The turquoise car swerves just left of the lens and its shadowed flank passes at arm's length, blocking the whole frame in darkness for a moment. All one shot.
rods4.ends_on: The car's dark flank covering the full frame at arm's length, a real wipe ready to open on the next shot as the car clears.
rods4.why: A locked camera at water height gives a near miss that only the car moves through, so the wipe comes from the car and not from a camera trick.

den2.motion: One continuous shot. The fist hauls the iron lever upward and the left end of the shelf lifts, tipping it steeper. The bottles slide down it one after another and drop into the black hatch, heavy glass rattling against glass, while the spilled liquor runs along the bar. The camera starts low, slides past the big amber bottle in the foreground and follows the last small clear bottle along the shelf. It tips over the lip and falls into the hatch, and the camera keeps pushing in until the hatch's black fills the whole frame. The coloured light on the wall stays still.
den2.ends_on: Full black inside the hatch after the last bottle falls, ready to cut to a round lamp or headlamp opening out of the dark.
den2.why: The camera chases one object through a chain reaction, which gives the shot speed and makes the bottle's fall the reason for the dark.

den3.motion: Camera locked overhead, one unbroken shot. Something out of sight bumps the green lamp shade at the top of the frame and it starts to swing on its cord, wider with each pass. The pool of light and the shadows of the hats sweep back and forth across the felt and the checkered floor, and the smoke tears around the moving shade. The six men stay seated with their hats down and faces hidden, their hands almost still. At about seven seconds the dark rim of the shade swings straight at the lens and covers the whole frame in black-green.
den3.ends_on: The shade's dark rim blocks the lens at the peak of its swing, with the moving shadow carrying the cut.
den3.why: All the motion comes from one swinging light, so the camera holds still and the men's hands have little chance to morph.

city1.motion: One continuous sideways move, gathering speed. Mist creeps over the water and the bars of light ripple. The tower, windows and lamps stay steady, and every building keeps its shape.
city1.ends_on: Dark girder steel across the whole frame, with the cut hidden on it.
city1.why: The prompt is kept short because the city is the weak spot, and parallax against a near girder gives speed without asking the skyline to do anything.

safe2.motion: Single tracking shot, camera low to the cobbles and moving with the safe at street speed. First three seconds: the yellow car pulls hard away, its rear squatting under the load, the chain snapping taut and the green iron safe jerking after it, scraping on its lower edge so the sparks spray from that edge only. Next three seconds: the safe slams over the bumps, the chain goes slack then taut, and the car rolls on its springs with its wheels on the ground, while the headlights far behind it grow closer. Last two seconds: the safe hits a raised ridge of cobbles, kicks up and lurches back at the lens until dark green iron fills the frame. Shop signs and the marquee stay soft with motion blur.
safe2.ends_on: Dark green iron filling the lens at the top of the safe's bounce, ready to cut to a dark shape of similar size moving out of the frame.
safe2.why: Timed beats build the weight through the chain's slack and pull, so the bounce at the end feels earned by the load.

safe3.motion: High on the rusted catwalk, watching from far away. Down below, the small car crosses the iron bridge from right to left, pulling a thin line of orange sparks behind it, and the headlights on the wet road behind it chase after it at a true, unhurried-looking distance speed, all of them staying on the road. Smoke rises slowly from the roofs and the city lights hold steady. The camera moves right along the catwalk in one continuous drift, the roofs shifting gently with parallax, and a dark steel upright of the railing passes close to the lens and covers the whole frame in black.
safe3.ends_on: The railing's dark upright blacks out the frame, replacing the suggested chimney because the railing is already in the start frame and nothing new has to appear.
safe3.why: The chase plays as a small detail seen from a distance, so the shot gets its scale from an onlooker's view rather than from action up close.
